compiled_state.title: As a skill author embedding a remediation loop, I want one shared protocol document defining cycle declarations, MAX_CYCLES bounds, termination tokens, oscillation-check hard gate, and HALT-vs-REPLAN exclusivity
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Author the shared workflow doc `skills/shared/workflows/remediation-loop-protocol.md` (per brainstorm savepoint Option A) and add the `planning.max_remediation_cycles=3` config key (minimum enforced >= 2). The protocol specifies: per-cycle "Current cycle: N of MAX_CYCLES" declaration, success-on-any-cycle behavior, REPLAN_ESCALATE: <upstream> on cycle MAX_CYCLES failure, /dso:oscillation-check as hard gate on cycle >= 2 with explicit OSCILLATION_CHECK_SKIPPED: <reason> escape, OSCILLATION_HALT on detected oscillation, and the structural exclusivity between HALT_FOR_USER and REPLAN_ESCALATE (REPLAN_ESCALATE only when cycle_count == MAX_CYCLES AND findings non-empty; other states emit PROTOCOL_ERROR). Also documents the DELTA OUTPUT template + token shared across SC1/SC2 producers.

**Why**: SC4 — the loop protocol is the spine referenced by every touchpoint embedding. Land first to avoid divergent inline embeddings.

**Scope**:
- IN: skills/shared/workflows/remediation-loop-protocol.md (protocol definition, tokens, exclusivity invariant, DELTA OUTPUT template)
- IN: plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (planning.max_remediation_cycles documentation with default 3 and enforced minimum >= 2)
- IN: Reusable protocol-conformance test harness (consumed by every touchpoint embedding story)
- IN: Upstream enum value definitions (brainstorm, preplanning, planner_supplied — see DD4 + the runtime-resolution consideration)
- OUT: Touchpoint embeddings themselves (delivered by SC4 touchpoint-embedding story)

## Done Definitions

- skills/shared/workflows/remediation-loop-protocol.md exists and defines the cycle-declaration string format, REPLAN_ESCALATE / HALT_FOR_USER / OSCILLATION_HALT / PROTOCOL_ERROR tokens, the oscillation-check hard-gate rule, the HALT-vs-REPLAN exclusivity invariant, and the DELTA OUTPUT template + token shared by SC1/SC2 producers
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- The config key planning.max_remediation_cycles is documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md with default 3 and an enforced minimum of 2; values < 2 are rejected at load time (not silently clamped)
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- A reusable protocol-conformance test harness exists that any touchpoint can invoke to assert: exactly MAX_CYCLES dispatches on forced failure, no cycle MAX_CYCLES+1, correct REPLAN_ESCALATE upstream token, OSCILLATION_HALT on detected oscillation, PROTOCOL_ERROR on illegal state transitions
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- The protocol document defines the upstream enum values (brainstorm, preplanning, planner_supplied) that the touchpoint-embedding story will reference
  ← Satisfies: sc-4

## Considerations

- [Architecture] This story produces a load-bearing shared doc; downstream stories (Phase E dispatch, impl-plan Steps 2/4/6 dispatch, sprint verifier-fail dispatch, touchpoint embeddings, cycles[] writer) all link to it. Land first to avoid divergent embeddings.
- [Risk] The min-enforced >= 2 rule must reject configuration at load time, not silently clamp; clamping would hide misconfiguration.
- [Contract / Dynamic upstream] The upstream enum must define canonical values: brainstorm, preplanning, planner_supplied. For the sprint verifier-fail touchpoint, the actual upstream is resolved at runtime from the verification-remediation-planner's escalation_upstream field — the protocol doc must specify that consumers MUST read this dynamically, never hardcode. Failure mode: hardcoded constant at sprint touchpoint silently overrides planner output.
- [Contract / DELTA OUTPUT] The DELTA OUTPUT template + token is documented here once and referenced by the SC1 and SC2 producer-contract stories; producer skill files MUST NOT redefine the template inline.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
